1_crop_portfolio.finding: Both players grew MELON as their primary crop simultaneously (us: 21-22 tiles day 3-20; opponent: 17-18 tiles day 0-20) -- crop CHOICE alone does not distinguish us from the opponent for most of the episode.
1_crop_portfolio.status: NOT SUPPORTED as the primary mechanism -- both chose the same crop

2_crop_timing.finding: Not separately isolated from selling timing (see #8) -- planting/harvest timing appeared similar (both had ~18-22 mature MELON tiles by day 8-10).

3_production_efficiency.finding: Comparable MELON tile counts (17-22 both sides) through day 20 -- no evidence of a large production-volume gap.
3_production_efficiency.status: NOT SUPPORTED as the primary mechanism

4_market_timing.finding: MERGED WITH #8 (selling) below -- this is where the evidence concentrated.

5_land_usage.finding: Both players stayed at 1 land quadrant for the entire episode (neither expanded). Land is NOT a factor in this specific loss.

6_fertilizer.finding: Not instrumented this session (would require per-action trace inspection beyond the daily-checkpoint trajectory built here).

7_capital_allocation.finding: Opponent's money stayed low ($1,400-2,500) through day 10, similar order of magnitude to ours ($0-3,000) -- no early capital advantage. The divergence appears suddenly at day 11 (see #8), not gradually.
7_capital_allocation.status: NOT SUPPORTED as an early/gradual mechanism -- ruled out as the cause of the INITIAL trajectory

8_inventory_selling.finding: EXPERIMENTALLY VALIDATED (this episode). The opponent's money jumped from $4,498 to $22,527 between day 11 hour 0 and hour 12 -- a single large bulk-sell event, timed while MELON price was still $129-250 (not yet crashed). The opponent then REPLANTED MELON back to 18 tiles and held for ~9 days while price recovered ($115->136), then executed a SECOND bulk-sell-and-exit at day 21-22 (tiles dropped 18->14->3->1, money jumped $24,172->$28,552), switching into CARROT -- right as price crashed again ($136->81->4). By contrast, OUR OWN MELON sell orders across the entire 720-turn episode numbered exactly TWO: 20 units at turn 265 (day 11, price already crashing $250->$129) and 95 units at turn 553 (day 23, price=$4 -- the exact bottom of the crash). The 95-unit dump at $4/unit realized roughly $380; the same 95 units at the day-8-10 price of ~$270 would have been worth roughly $25,650 -- a difference exceeding our entire loss margin ($30,210) on its own.
8_inventory_selling.status: EXPERIMENTALLY VALIDATED for this episode -- root cause identified with turn-level precision

9_resource_conversion_efficiency.finding: Not separately measured -- effectively subsumed by #8 (the loss is in REALIZED PRICE per unit sold, not units produced).

10_combinations_interactions.finding: The mechanism is fundamentally an INTERACTION: both players flood the same MELON market, but the opponent's selling is TIMED to extract value before/during the crash their own volume (and ours) causes, while ours is timed into the trough (whether by threshold-mode holding too long, or by shed-capacity-driven forced dumping -- both plausible given only 2 sell events across 720 turns, not distinguished this session).
10_combinations_interactions.status: This IS the mechanism -- see conclusion

distinct_from_prior_findings: Distinct from Phase 3.4's self_inflicted_narrow_market_price_crash (which is about PRODUCTION VOLUME crashing a market) and from F-001 (labor/animal resource scaling). This is specifically about WHEN inventory is converted to cash relative to the price trajectory -- a genuinely new, precisely evidenced mechanism.
generalization_status: HYPOTHESIS beyond this single episode -- the OTHER 2 F-003 episodes from Submission A (104570723, 104615545) were not re-examined with this same turn-level selling-timing lens this session; whether the same mechanism explains them is UNKNOWN pending that analysis.
countermeasure_status: NOT BUILT OR TESTED this phase, per the brief's explicit instruction: 'Do not create a detector until the underlying mechanism is sufficiently supported.' The mechanism is now well-supported for this one episode; a countermeasure (e.g. a smarter batch-sell-timing policy) would require its own design + controlled validation cycle, appropriately deferred to Phase 3.7.
final_classification: UNRESOLVED F-003, WITH A PRECISELY IDENTIFIED MECHANISM FOR THE PRIMARY CASE STUDY -- narrowed significantly from Phase 3.5's vague 'crop choice' hypothesis, not yet generalized or fixed.
